newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Denktash says Cyprus missile deal hinders talks.
newsitem.headline: Denktash says Cyprus missile deal hinders talks.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash said on Monday that a Cypriot government decision to buy Russian surface-to-air missiles hindered any negotiated settlement to the Cyprus issue.

"As time goes on and the Greek Cypriot leadership tells its population that they are now ready even to tackle Turkey if need be, less and less chances can be seen for a negotiated process," he told Reuters.
Denktash, the leader of a breakaway state recognised only by Turkey, said the planned purchase of the S-300 missile system was a threat to the island's Turkish Cypriots.
"The danger to us is not an imminent physical danger, it is a threat," he said. Diplomats say the missiles, with a range of 150 km (90 miles), could knock out planes in Turkish air space.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 in response to a coup engineered by the military government then ruling Greece. Some 30,000 Turkish troops are stationed on Cyprus.
Efforts over the years by the United Nations, the United States and the European Union have all failed to resolve the division of the Mediterranean island.
Denktash said the EU's decision to hold membership talks next year with the Cypriot government had raised tension.
"It has also encouraged the Greek Cypriots to proceed on the wrong track by insisting on arms and armaments, on missiles etc," he said.

Cyprus is already one of the most heavily militarised areas of the world. Denktash said a recent Greek Cypriot weapons buildup and foreign backing for the government increased the possibility of conflict.
"If they feel that they have got Russia behind them, that Europe is behind them (and) that their propaganda has succeeded...then I am sure they will start something," he said.
